/quiz: Answer questions, review feedback and move through a quiz.
/quizgame: Practise a topic through quiz challenges.
/memorygame: Find matching pairs by revealing hidden cards.
/jeopardy: Choose clues, reveal answers and assess your recall.
/crossword: Revise key terms by completing a crossword.
/mindmap: Organise a topic into branches and relationships.
/fillintheblanks: Complete missing terms and check your answers.

/eli5: Request a simple explanation with familiar examples.
/sortinggame: Classify examples into categories and check the result.
/conceptquiz: Check conceptual understanding through questions and explanations.
/summary: Condense a source into its main ideas.
/languagedrill: Practise terminology by completing and checking sentences.
/blueprint: Outline the structure and components of a project or idea.
/multiplechoice: Choose answers from options and check your score.
/recall: Attempt an answer before revealing it and assess your recall.
/gapfinder: Use diagnostic questions to identify gaps in understanding.
/blackboard: Work through a board-style explanation with answer checks.
/whiteboard: Arrange ideas and explanations on a whiteboard-style layout.
/sketchnote: Combine concise notes, keywords and visual cues.
/flowchart: Represent a process as connected steps and decisions.
/infographic: Present key information in a concise visual layout.
/timeline: Place events or stages in chronological order.
/venn: Compare shared and distinct features of concepts.
/analogy: Explain a concept through a comparison, including its limits.
/comic: Explain a topic through a short sequence of story panels.
/feynman: Explain an idea simply, identify gaps and revise the explanation.
/glossary: Collect key terms with brief definitions.

/studyplan: Break a learning goal into activities and track completion.
/checklist: Turn a task into items you can check and track.
/pomodoro: Organise study sessions and breaks, then mark completion.

/pyramid: Arrange ideas into levels of a hierarchy.
/tree: Organise a topic into a branching hierarchy.
/anatomydiagram: Break a system into parts and explain their roles.
/cyclediagram: Represent the stages of a repeating process.
/explodedview: Separate a system into components to show how they fit together.
/handwritten: Request notes presented in a handwritten style.
/decisionmatrix: Compare options against criteria, with checks to reveal.
/onepager: Condense a topic into a single-page overview.
/labeleddiagram: Identify the parts of a diagram with explanatory labels.
/mnemonic: Create a memorable cue for recalling information.
/memorypalaceimage: Associate information with locations in an imagined space.
/memoryhooks: Connect unfamiliar ideas to memorable associations.
/mnemonicart: Turn memory cues into a visual composition.
/emojisummary: Summarise key ideas using short text and emoji cues.
/cheatsheet: Collect essential facts, rules and formulas for quick reference.
/deepdive: Explore a topic in greater depth with details and connections.
/mistakelog: Record misconceptions, review corrections and track progress.
/stepbystep: Break an explanation or task into ordered steps.
/twinexample: Compare two related examples to reveal an important distinction.
/workedexample: Study a complete solution with its intermediate steps.

/rubric: Describe assessment criteria and levels of performance.
/bloomquestions: Explore a topic through questions at different cognitive levels.
/questionbank: Build a set of practice questions with answers to reveal.
/flippedclassroom: Plan preparation before class and application during class.
/differentiate: Adapt an activity's supports and difficulty to learning needs.

/peerassessment: Review a peer's work using shared criteria and scores.

/learningstations: Organise activities into stations and track completion.
/slides: Outline a sequence of presentation slides.
